pr_title: loqrecovery: add replica info collection to admin server
pr_body:
This commit adds replica info and range descriptor collection from partially available cluster that lost quorum on some ranges. Collection is done using AdminServer calls. Cluster wide call performs fan-out using node info from gossip. Local replica info collection on nodes is done by scanning storages.

Release note: File format used for transient loss of quorum recovery files has changed. It is not possible to use replica info files generated by earlier versions to be used with current and future versions.

Fixes #93040

Note that we recovery doesn't need collect command to be "remote capable" but allowing this makes development and debugging simpler as you can create local snapshot from a cluster that you can subsequently verify you planning against.

Touches #74135

issue_context.title: loqrecovery: add replica info collector
issue_context.body:
Add implementation of collection rpc in Admin as per [RFC](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/master/docs/RFCS/20221101_half_online_loss_of_quorum_recovery.md?rgh-link-date=2022-12-05T15%3A16%3A15Z):

Collection should do a best effort collection of range descriptor metadata about all ranges. This full or partial info should be streamed back to caller.
Collection should use fanout to nodes discovered via gossip to collect replica info and stream info back to caller.
It should tolerate any partial failures and send only available info.

Depends on changes to plan protobuf definition in https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/93037

Part of https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/77273


Jira issue: CRDB-22129

Epic CRDB-14205

review_comments: We should consider extending the data-driven tests to use online recovery, but this will do for now. Add an issue for it?
Discussed elsewhere, doesn't make sense to involve RPC servers in the tests that check the core recovery protocol.
Consider mentioning why we enforce a server-side timeout here instead of using a client-side timeout: because we want this to work even when the meta ranges are unavailable.

How does this interact with retryable transaction errors? Are they automatically retried, and if so, will `txn.Iterate()` emit duplicates? If not, will this be flaky in the face of retryable errors, since we don't handle them?
This should also be handled by setting timestamp. We should only be getting non retryable errors here and we are fine then, no duplicates.

We should look closer at the implications of this transaction, to ensure it doesn't cause problems with concurrent writes. We've seen indications elsewhere (e.g. below-Raft migrations) that long-running meta scans can be problematic.

I think we should be ok with only making reads and having fixed timestamp which will prevent restarts and ignore updates.
Making it non transactional would partially defeat the purpose of us reading metadata. Anything you have in mind to make it less disruptive?
If we're certain that this doesn't contend with concurrent writers then it should be fine.
Should this check for and reject/merge duplicate nodes?

I was looking on existing helpers that we have in netutil/net.go and grpcutil/grpc_util.go and came to a conclusion that they don't distinguish between unavailable nodes and failing nodes, cancelled contexts. But I think it is more important in our case as we want to separate unavailable node from the rest of flakiness or unhealthy nodes. Unavailable as a result of dial seem to be closest to unretriable error. Any other error is worth retrying and failing after.
We also don't care about interrupted connections as we aren't reusing them.
Ok, as long as we're handling the errors we need.
